subject: Pack interchangeability, smoothing corridor, and Exhibit B redlines
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@peregrineanalytics.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-11-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Exhibit B: pack interchange and floor smoothing

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an order form I wanted to clarify a couple of items in Exhibit B (pricing schedule) that are blockers for our procurement team. Attached is a small procurement_profile.csv that shows our expected SKU mix across Q1–Q4.

Two main asks:
1) Pack interchangeability: we often re-balance SKU mix across bundles mid-quarter. We'd like an explicit mechanism that allows moving up to 15% of committed units between SKUs in the same package family without triggering a full true-up or additional surcharge.
2) Floor smoothing: with seasonal spikes we want a smoothing corridor so we don't get hit by the floor immediately after a one-off pilot. Something like a 60-day smoothing window or an annual true-up.

Can Redwood accept language for a limited pack-interchange credit and a smoothing corridor? If not, what are the suggested guardrails you would need?

Best,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement, Peregrine Analytics
Attachments: procurement_profile.csv (CSV)

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@peregrineanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-11-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B: pack interchange and floor smoothing

Tom —

Really helpful note and thanks for the profile. I think we can get to a compromise that preserves your operational flexibility without materially increasing revenue leakage for Redwood. High level:

- Pack interchange: we can propose a limited "pack pooling" credit where up to 15% of committed units can shift within a defined family per quarter, tracked via a sentinel SKU. Any overage beyond that would be handled in the regular true-up.
- Smoothing corridor: propose a 60-day smoothing window for seasonal variance, with an annual true-up to reconcile any sustained shortfalls.

I'm attaching a quick working draft of an amended order schedule (markus_proposed_order_schedule_v1.pdf) with markup callouts for the two clauses. Could you confirm whether a quarterly or monthly tracking cadence works for your side?

If that looks reasonable, I'll loop in legal for precise language.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: markus_proposed_order_schedule_v1.pdf (PDF)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-11-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B: pack interchange and floor smoothing

Markus / Tom (cc'd) —

Product POV, short: pack pooling is fine if we keep both (a) a sentinel SKU to ensure volumes are tracked; and (b) a cap on interchange credits that phases down if overall committed dollar run rate drops more than 10% year-over-year. Operational notes:

- Sentinel SKU approach: pick one SKU per family; all adjustments route through that identifier so billing aligns with telemetry.
- Credit cap: interchange credits accrue but cannot exceed 20% of the floor protection in any quarter. This prevents large negative adjustments.
- True-up cadence: quarterly reporting is easiest for customers on your scale; we can waive monthly reporting for initial 2 quarters to reduce noise.

I uploaded a small note (karthik_pack_notes.txt) with examples. Happy to join a call to walk the procurement team through tradeoffs.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
Attachments: karthik_pack_notes.txt (TXT)

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com

Subject: Fwd: Questions on Exhibit B — please review and propose legal language

Irene —

Forwarding Tom's ask and Karthik's product suggestions. Can you please review the attached draft (markus_proposed_order_schedule_v1.pdf) and propose redlines for Exhibit B that:

- Provide a clear definition for "pack family" and "sentinel SKU";
- Add a pack-interchange credit mechanism limited to 15% per quarter with a quarterly cap (we suggested 20% of floor protection);
- Define a 60-day smoothing corridor and an annual true-up process;
- Include supplier-friendly audit rights and an explicit set-off mechanism for interchange credits against future invoices (we need a cap to avoid negative invoices).

If helpful, we can loop Alexis Garcia (external counsel) for a slightly accelerated review — Tom's procurement is pushing to finalize language this month.

Thanks,
Markus

Markus / team / Tom —

Thanks for the clear requests and the draft. I reviewed and proposed redlines; high-level summary below and attached the marked PDF (legal_markups_exhibitB_redlined.pdf).

Accepted in principle:
- "Pack family" and "sentinel SKU" definitions: OK, but define sentinel SKU as an accounting identifier that must map to telemetry within 10 business days for reconciliation.
- 15% per-quarter pack-interchange allowance: acceptable with an annual cap. We propose the interchange credit cannot exceed 15% of the annual floor protection amount and cannot create a negative invoice (i.e., credits offset future invoices only, up to invoice value).

Required changes / alternatives:
- Smoothing corridor: 60 days is operationally fine, but replace one-off language with an "annual reconciliation window" clause (customer must perform an annual true-up within 30 days of fiscal year-end). The smoothing corridor will be an operational tolerance used only for interim reporting; final settlement occurs at annual true-up.
- Credit accrual & audit: require quarterly statements and a 90-day audit window post-annual-true-up. Interchange credits that are disputed must be raised within 30 days of the quarterly statement.
- Cap phase-down: we will accept a phase-down if tied to a defined drop in committed $ run rate (propose >10% YoY decline) but the formula must be specified in Exhibit B (we added a simple matrix in the redline).

Next steps:
1) If Tom's team is comfortable with the annual true-up + smoothing tolerance model, confirm and we'll finalize language.
2) We will run this by Alexis (cc'd) for procurement-side counsel alignment; if Alexis approves we can generate a final order form and DocuSign packet.

Attached: legal_markups_exhibitB_redlined.pdf (PDF)

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
